findings.title: Terminal forward cleanup authority bypasses rollback preflight
findings.observation: The Cycle 4 preflight returns null for every terminal RESTORE lifecycle before resolving that lifecycle's own FORWARD_RESTORE_CLEANUP reference. executeRollbackWithCleanup then performs application rollback and production cleanup before cleanupOwnedProject finally resolves the terminal reference.
findings.trigger: Begin actual rollback from a valid RESTORE CLEANED lifecycle whose cleanupReference names forward-restore-cleanup.json, then make that fixed-path record malformed, digest-invalid or wrong-bound.
findings.impact: Irreversible rollback work and production Docker deletion can occur before the authoritative restore evidence is rejected. This violates the accepted fail-closed ordering and can leave production removed plus rollback aggregate evidence written even though terminal restore authority is corrupt.

evidence.description: Terminal lifecycle states return null before forwardFile is derived or parsed; application rollback and production cleanup immediately follow the preflight.

A fresh-context exact-head reproduction created a legitimate CLEANED forward lifecycle, corrupted forward-restore-cleanup.json to malformed JSON, then invoked executeRollbackWithCleanup. It observed one application rollback call, three new production deletes, no production resources remaining and rollback-cleanup.json written before rejection.
The new rejection matrix leaves RESTORE in QUIESCING with cleanupReference=null; no committed case exercises corrupted evidence referenced by a terminal lifecycle.

The design and operations guide require malformed, digest-invalid, wrong-bound, wrong-state or authority-conflicting forward evidence to abort before application rollback, Docker deletion or aggregate evidence.

findings.remediation: Do not return from the preflight solely because the lifecycle is terminal. Resolve and verify the terminal lifecycle's own cleanupReference before any rollback side effect, require FORWARD_RESTORE_CLEANUP to match the fixed path, exact attempt/project/database/result/digest and terminal lifecycle authority, verify the live restore project remains empty for PASS, and only then reuse the exact result. Reject malformed, wrong-bound or inconsistent terminal authority before application rollback or production cleanup.
findings.verification: Add actual-rollback regressions for CLEANED and CLEANUP_FAILED restore lifecycles with exact valid, malformed and wrong-bound lifecycle-referenced forward evidence. Valid authority must be reused without restore deletion; invalid authority must produce zero application rollback calls, zero new Docker deletes, no rollback-cleanup.json and no terminal success evidence.

findings.title: Deletion-before-evidence crash is replayable through actual rollback
findings.observation: The current implementation detects only RESTORE QUIESCING with a nonempty frozen set and an empty exact live project, derives the same removal-argument digest from the frozen authority, then requires consecutive empty samples without issuing another delete.
findings.trigger: The process dies after completing the frozen restore deletion but before forward-restore-cleanup.json is written, then actual rollback resumes with no forward evidence.
findings.impact: The prior safe-but-unrecoverable empty state now completes to PASS, CLEANED and terminal ROLLED_BACK rather than CLEANUP_FAILED and ROLLBACK_FAILED.
